plans.note: Section 21 is the operative cap; check mutuality, multiple-of-fees quantum, exclusion of indirect damages, and whether the 'Excluded Claims' definition in Section 1 carves out IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach, and willful misconduct. Cross-check Sections 20 (indemnity) and 15/17 (data/security) for super-caps.

Section 20 should contain a Vendor IP infringement indemnity plus indemnity for Vendor misconduct and data/security breach; confirm any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data legality/use only) and uncapped or super-capped treatment aligns with Section 21.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan Sections 2 (scope), 12 (Customer responsibilities) and 30 (General) for any covenant limiting our businesses, competing products, or in-house build rights before concluding absent.

Watch for sole-source or 'preferred supplier' language embedded in Section 2 (Agreement Structure and Scope), Section 4 (Order Forms and Affiliate Orders) or Section 12; flag only if it restricts purchasing from other suppliers.

Direction check: an MFN would most likely sit in Section 7 (Fees) or Section 4 (Order Forms). Accept MFN running in our favour; object only if we must extend best terms or benchmark pricing to the Vendor.

Non-solicits typically appear in General (Section 30) or alongside personnel/confidentiality provisions; if present, confirm mutuality, 12-month cap, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 9 governs termination rights; confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on ~30 days' notice without early-termination fees, and that any Vendor convenience right is removed or limited to end of term (cross-check Sections 8 and 10 for penalties).
Section 8 (Term and Renewal): test auto-renewal length, non-renewal notice window (target 30 days, no more than 60) and any uplift cap on renewal Fees, which may cross-reference Section 7.

Section 28: verify law is New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts in that jurisdiction rather than offshore or ICC/foreign-seat arbitration; note the Vendor is a UK entity so England and Wales courts are an acceptable fallback.

Section 24: secure our right to assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and delete any Vendor termination or repricing right triggered by our change of control.

Direction check in Section 14: Deliverables paid for should vest in Customer (or at minimum a broad perpetual licence); Section 15 must confirm Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data with no Vendor ownership, and check Section 13 for any grant-back of our IP or data (e.g., aggregated/derived data or feedback assignment).

Section 13 (Access Rights and Licence): extend scope to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, delete 'revocable at will'/unilateral suspension language, and confirm the 'Vendor Technology' definition in Section 1 does not narrow the grant.

Section 22 covers audits of our usage: limit to once per 12 months, 10+ business days' written notice, business hours, remote/off-site records review where possible, Vendor's cost absent material underpayment, and NDA protection. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) may carry related record-keeping duties on us.

Direction check: retain any service credits owed to us in Section 3/SLA, but resist liquidated damages, early-termination charges or interest/penalty amounts payable by us in Sections 7 and 9; confirm Section 21 does not exclude credits as our remedy.

Section 19: seek a professional/conforming-services warranty of at least 90 days (ongoing for subscription Services) with re-performance, repair or refund as remedy; check Section 6 (Acceptance) and Section 3 for shorter windows or 'sole remedy' language and any broad disclaimer.

Section 18 exists; confirm it specifies commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O, cyber liability and workers' comp with adequate limits, certificates on request and notice of cancellation, given Vendor hosts Customer Data (Sections 15 and 17).

Check Section 4 (Order Forms) and Section 7 (Fees) for take-or-pay, minimum volume or non-reducible commitment language and any prohibition on decreasing quantities at renewal (Section 8); if present, pair with a termination-for-convenience exit.

Section 11 addresses transition and data return; verify a defined assistance period (e.g., 90 days at then-current rates, extendable), export of Customer Data in a usable format, deletion certification, and that Section 10 does not condition return on payment of disputed amounts.
